chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

Whichever woman or man, being fearful, departs from the Sacred Monument (Muzdalifah) at night, there is no problem; let him pelt the Jamarah, then let him proceed and instruct someone to sacrifice on his behalf; and the woman shortens (her hair), and the man shaves (his head). Then let him perform Tawaf by the House (Kaaba) and by As-Safa and Al-Marwa, then let him return to Mina. So if he goes to Mina and no sacrifice has been made on his behalf, there is no problem if he sacrifices himself, and let him carry the hair when he shaves in Mecca to Mina; and if he wishes, he may shorten (his hair) if he had performed Hajj before that.
ai.seo_question: What are the ritual steps for a pilgrim who departs Muzdalifah at night due to fear?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'Qada al-Hajj' (making up the Hajj) for those who depart Muzdalifah before dawn due to fear or necessity, a ruling derived from the Prophet's practice. It establishes a streamlined ritual sequence—Jamarah, Tawaf, Sa'i, and sacrifice—emphasizing that the core validity of Hajj is preserved despite the early departure, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in ritual obligations. The text also addresses practical details like hair cutting and the location of sacrifice, reinforcing the flexibility within the structured rites of Hajj.
